raw_response:
I have been working this land since I was a small child alongside my father and grandfather. The wheat-maize rotation is what my family has always done here in Quzhou, and it is what the land and the water situation call for. With some of my family members gone to the city for work, I need to manage the fields mostly by myself, so I cannot afford to do things that waste my time or money.

**My thinking for wheat:**
I plant all 10.1 mu to wheat in October after the maize comes off. I buy improved seed from the village supply store — same variety I have used for years, not hybrid, that is not how we do wheat here. I split my fertilizer: base application before sowing, then top-dress at jointing. I run the well three times — once in winter to protect the roots when it gets cold and dry, once at jointing, once during grain filling. Rust and powdery mildew always come around heading time, so I spray twice.

**My thinking for maize:**
Right after wheat harvest in June, the same 10.1 mu goes to maize. Everyone in my village switched to hybrid seed years ago and so did I — the yields are just better. Maize needs a lot of fertilizer. I apply base fertilizer at planting and chase it with a top-dress around topping time. Summer gets rain sometimes, but I keep the well ready and irrigate twice to be safe — once at planting if it is dry, once at silking. I spray herbicide early so the weeds do not get ahead of me.
